neighbours.label: the comma closing a fronted 'When <someone> took office / came to the throne,' clause; also ' as' after 'quoted'
fire: Roosevelt inherited a country in crisis. When he took office, a quarter of the workforce was unemployed.
The young queen was only eighteen. When she ascended the throne, the treasury was nearly empty.
The new manager had never run a factory. When he took charge, he found the machines in poor repair.
Thatcher led the party for four years in opposition. When she became prime minister, inflation stood at ten percent.
A senior police officer is quoted as saying that the investigation is far from over.
The general arrived in the spring. When he assumed command, he discovered that supplies were low.
In the article the coach is quoted as saying that the team needs two new defenders.
Lincoln won the election in November. By the time he was sworn in, seven states had seceded.
